service: CPAP device for obstructive sleep apnea
vignette: 58-year-old man. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by his physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. Attended polysomnography in a sleep laboratory showed an AHI of 22 events/hour over 6.5 hours of sleep. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The sleep test was ordered by his treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before he began using the device.
rationale_note: Typical qualifying case: AHI 22 on attended PSG.

service: CPAP device for obstructive sleep apnea
vignette: 67-year-old woman with documented hypertension on two medications. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by her physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. Unattended home sleep test with a Type III device showed an AHI of 9 events/hour. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The sleep test was ordered by her treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before she began using the device.
rationale_note: AHI 9 (5-14 band) qualifies because hypertension is documented.

service: CPAP device for obstructive sleep apnea
vignette: 72-year-old man without hypertension, heart disease, or stroke; he denies daytime sleepiness. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by his physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. Attended PSG showed an AHI of 15.0 events/hour over 7 hours of sleep. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The sleep test was ordered by his treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before he began using the device.
rationale_note: Boundary: AHI exactly 15 qualifies without symptoms or comorbidities (>= 15).

service: CPAP device for obstructive sleep apnea
vignette: 61-year-old man. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by his physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. He denies daytime sleepiness, insomnia, mood or memory problems; blood pressure is normal and he has no history of heart disease or stroke. Type III home sleep test showed an AHI of 9 events/hour. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The sleep test was ordered by his treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before he began using the device.
rationale_note: AHI 9 with no qualifying symptom or comorbidity documented.

service: CPAP device for obstructive sleep apnea
vignette: 64-year-old woman. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by her physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. Overnight pulse oximetry at home showed an oxygen desaturation index of 25 events/hour. No polysomnography or home sleep apnea test was performed. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The oximetry was ordered by her treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before she began using the device.
rationale_note: Overnight pulse oximetry alone is not a qualifying test.

service: CPAP device for obstructive sleep apnea
vignette: 59-year-old man. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by his physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. Unattended home sleep test with a Type IV device recording 2 channels (oximetry and heart rate) reported an AHI of 28 events/hour. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The sleep test was ordered by his treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before he began using the device.
rationale_note: Type IV device with only 2 channels does not qualify (needs at least 3).

service: CPAP device for obstructive sleep apnea
vignette: 70-year-old woman with no hypertension, heart disease, stroke, or sleep-related symptoms documented. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by her physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. Attended PSG recorded only 1.5 hours of continuous sleep with 25 apneas and hypopneas in total (reported AHI 16.7 events/hour). Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The sleep test was ordered by her treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before she began using the device.
rationale_note: 1.5 h of sleep with 25 events: AHI 16.7, but 2 h at >=15/h requires >=30 events.

service: CPAP device for obstructive sleep apnea
vignette: 63-year-old man. Attended PSG ordered by his treating physician showed an AHI of 31 events/hour. The record contains the sleep study report and CPAP order, but no clinical evaluation by a physician. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before he began using the device.
rationale_note: Qualifying test but no clinical evaluation in the record.

service: CPAP device for obstructive sleep apnea
vignette: 66-year-old man diagnosed with OSA (AHI 24 on attended PSG after a documented clinical evaluation) who completed the initial 12-week CPAP period. He used the device on only a few nights, reports no improvement in sleepiness, and his physician documents no clinical benefit from CPAP. Requesting continued CPAP coverage beyond 12 weeks. The sleep test was ordered by his treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. The DME supplier documented education on proper CPAP use before he began using the device.
rationale_note: Continued coverage after 12 weeks requires benefit; physician documents none.

service: CPAP device for obstructive sleep apnea
vignette: 78-year-old man with mild dementia who lives with his daughter, who is home every night and was trained by the DME supplier to operate the CPAP device safely. Face-to-face clinical evaluation by his physician documented snoring and witnessed apneas. Attended PSG showed an AHI of 34 events/hour. The sleep test was ordered by his treating physician and performed under appropriate physician supervision. Requesting an initial 12-week CPAP period.
rationale_note: Caregiver compensates for patient's limited capacity (allowed by C2).
